Hi Rachel,

Hope you’re well. Ingenium’s security and legal teams are compiling evidence for an internal review ahead of our pilot procurement. We have a short set of questions about how Redwood handles customer prompts and responses in the context of model training and retention. Could you please confirm/provide: 

- Whether Redwood uses customer prompts, completions, or embeddings to train or fine-tune public or internal models (ever / by default / with opt-in).
- Default retention period for prompt/response logs for Hosted API customers and what data is retained (request/response, metadata, IP, headers).
- Options for disabling storage or shortening retention (self-serve vs. enterprise contract).
- For Dedicated and Private deployments: whether Redwood ever has access to customer data or uses it for training.
- Where to find signed DPA clauses, SCCs (if relevant), SOC 2 evidence, and a short SIG/CAIQ answer set for the above topics.

If convenient, attach any short artifacts (SOC 2 summary, DPA excerpt, retention policy). We’re aiming to get everything to our privacy committee by Monday 30 Nov.

Thanks — appreciate a quick acknowledgment and an ETA.

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Acknowledged; we’ll assemble the materials and a short summary. 

Quick answers up-front so your reviewers have something immediately:
- Redwood does not incorporate customer prompt/response content into model training or model weights for public models.
- Default hosted-log retention is 30 days for debugging, abuse detection, and caching; retained items are request/response text, timestamps, and routing metadata (IP is redacted for stored logs).
- Enterprise customers can request shorter retention or opt-out of hosted logs via contract; Dedicated & Private deployments keep data within customer VPC/cluster and Redwood does not ingest that data for training.

I’m looping in Stephanie (Privacy & Solutions) and Sergio (Legal) to provide the formal artifacts (SOC 2 summary, DPA excerpt, SIG/CAIQ answers, and our retention policy). We should have a package by EOD Friday.

Would you prefer artifacts delivered via your secure Drive link or via NDA-protected upload?

Hi Samantha — thanks for reaching out. I pulled together the short summary below and attached the artifacts referenced (SOC 2 summary, DPA excerpt, SIG answers, and our logging & retention policy). Please find a concise answer set for the items you listed: 

1) Do we use customer prompts/responses to train models?
- Short answer: No. Redwood does not use customer prompt/response text to train, fine-tune, or improve public or internal models. This applies to hosted API usage and is enforced by our ingestion and model-training policies.
- Notes: We do maintain separate model onboarding processes where vendors or partners may contribute datasets, but those are isolated and subject to explicit agreements and review; customer-provided production traffic is not part of that pipeline.

2) Default retention and retained fields (Hosted API):
- Default retention: 30 days for text and routing metadata.
- Retained fields: request timestamp, model requested, request text (prompt), response text (completion), request id/correlation id, and routing metadata (region, model variant).
- IP addresses are redacted before long-term storage; ephemeral logs for troubleshooting may contain transient IPs but are not used for analytics or training.

3) Opt-out / retention configuration:
- Self-service: Customers can enable reduced telemetry via the Console to reduce logs for non-production keys.
- Enterprise: Contractual options to shorten retention to as low as 0 days or to disable storage of prompts/responses; available as an enterprise add-on. We capture these choices in the DPA and customer-specific security appendix.

4) Dedicated / Private deployments:
- Dedicated: Data remains in a dedicated pool; Redwood operational staff have limited access under strict controls. We explicitly exclude using this data for model training in the contract.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer-managed environment — Redwood does not collect or use any customer data for training unless explicitly engaged under a separate data collaboration agreement.

5) Evidence and artifacts provided: 
- redwood_dpa_excerpt.pdf (DPA clauses describing data usage and opt-out paths)
- SOC2-TypeII-summary-2026.pdf (high-level SOC 2 attest summary; full report available under NDA)
- SIG-excerpt-answers.pdf (selected CAIQ/SIG responses for LLM data handling)
- logging_and_retention_policy.txt (operational retention & redaction practices)

If it helps, we can also provide a short snippet for your DPIA that you can paste into your template — outlining risk mitigations around data separation, pseudonymization, and access control. Let me know if you want that.

I’ll also add the canonical wording we include in our DPA and security appendix in a follow-up note for your legal team to place into procurement paperwork.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Privacy & Solutions, Redwood Inference
